facts.fact: The Ministry of Health's bulletin for July to September 2023 states that the ministry decided to use DHIS2 as the exclusive national HMIS platform for routine health information, run by its HMIS Section, with no other vertical health data collection allowed.

The bulletin states that the ministry's Health Information Section and its partners prepared and finalised a five-year costed Health Information Strategy, and that HSSP III and the Investment Case 2022-2027 set DHIS2 as the single national reporting platform; no date of finalisation is given, so the bulletin's quarter is used.

The ministry reports 579 public health facilities reporting to DHIS2 in July to September 2023, against 532 in the same quarter of 2022, on data sets for health-centre outpatients and hospital outpatients and inpatients, at an aggregate reporting rate of 95.8% (86.8% in Q3 2022); it gives no breakdown by hospital level or facility type, and puts private hospitals' reporting rate at 2%.
The bulletin states that the ministry's HMIS section initiated the pilot of electronic health records, on RAAD EMR, in partnership with SPIDER (July to September 2023).
The bulletin states that the electronic health records pilot is supported by the Government of Sweden through SPIDER (July to September 2023).

The ministry states that the electronic health records pilot has been launched in two health facilities in Banadir, where RAAD EMR is installed and integrated with the HMIS on DHIS2, with Galmudug and Puntland planned next; the facilities' type is not given (July to September 2023).

The tiers value reads hospital and health-centre data sets as T1 to T3 without the document splitting hospital levels; health posts are not named.
